clue.text: Songs of enchanting female

definitions.meaning: rhythmic Caribbean songs, often topical and improvised
belonging to Calypso, the nymph who held Odysseus spellbound on her island, written with an apostrophe s

explanation.surface: A siren's repertoire: the songs sung by some bewitching woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is the possessive CALYPSO'S: Calypso is the nymph of the Odyssey who kept Odysseus captive for seven years.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the Trinidadian song form, matching the plural noun in the clue.

clue.text: Boast: sent in to mobilise uncommitted voters

indicators.note: to mobilise is to set in motion, so the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A rallying cry: brag about sending canvassers in to get the floating voters moving.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: abstentions are strictly the votes withheld by those who stay uncommitted, standing here for the voters themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who decline to back either side register abstentions rather than votes, a metonymy for the undecided.

clue.text: See 7
See 19
Group with tenor was first to get paid

parts.note: a set is a group of things or people
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music
to lead is to be first, so 'was first' is led

explanation.surface: A band with a tenor who topped the bill gets its fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A settled bill is one that has been paid off, an accounting sense.

clue.text: Reject berth on ship and get off

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another simply comes first
to reject is to throw back, so the word for a berth is turned round

parts.note: a berth is a bed on a ship or train
the ark is Noah's ship

explanation.surface: A passenger turns down the cabin offered and simply disembarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reject' looks like the definition's partner, but it only signals turning the berth word round; 'on' puts it first in an across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To debark is to disembark, leaving a ship or aircraft.

clue.text: Assume I can't possibly keep quiet and remain calm

parts.note: to don is to put on or assume clothing or a manner

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the scrambled letters hold the quiet sign inside them
possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone protests that keeping silent and staying composed is beyond them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges I CANT into TANIC, which holds P to give TPANIC after DON.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the stock instruction to stay composed, which is what remaining calm means.

clue.text: Live nude — one way it aroused 16 in private

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: aroused means stirred up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: A racy confession about naked goings-on that are best kept quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aroused' rearranges NUDE ONE WAY IT into TWEEN YOU AND I. 16 is SOLECISTIC: the phrase is a classic grammatical slip, since a preposition should take 'me'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means confidentially, said privately, and is the famous ungrammatical version of the idiom.

clue.text: Talk of sport — manager missing second half

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: missing its second half means only the first half of the manager's name is kept

parts.note: Jose Mourinho is a famous football manager

explanation.surface: Gossip around a sports club whose boss has walked out at half-time.
explanation.walkthrough: Mourinho has eight letters; dropping the last four leaves MOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumour is idle talk or hearsay passed around.

clue.text: Seeing that country going back on promise

parts.note: as can mean since or seeing that

indicators.note: going back means the country's letters are written backwards

parts.note: US is the United States
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A nation is accused of reneging on a pledge it made.
explanation.definitionFit: To assure someone is to promise or guarantee them something.

clue.text: 16 sign for shoppers of sorts — one element's wrong

indicators.note: wrong signals letters put into a mistaken order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the letters of the word are used as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A shop notice with something incorrect in it, which is exactly the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is SOLECISTIC: the supermarket checkout sign should strictly say 'fewer', not 'less'.
explanation.definitionFit: Express checkout lanes carry this notice, a famous grammatical error displayed to customers.

clue.text: Fancy Ant alone of new arrivals

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters are dressed up anew

explanation.surface: A lone ant described as fancy, oddly linked to newcomers.
explanation.definitionFit: Neonatal relates to newborns, the newest arrivals in the world.

clue.text: God welcomes each song of praise

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the god holds the other letters

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: A deity receives every hymn sung in their honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A paean is a hymn or song of triumph or thanksgiving.

clue.text: See 15
Get in essentials taking uniform in case

indicators.note: taking means holding, so the core letters hold the other one
the essentials are the core, so the outer letters of the two words are discarded

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Pack the basics, including your uniform, into a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: The core of GET IN is ETI, which takes U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles or cosmetics.

clue.text: Day ahead: detention … cane — duo, frustrated, make 16 claim

parts.note: Wed is short for Wednesday
on can mean ahead or forward, as in 'go on'

indicators.note: frustrated means thwarted and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Two pupils, fed up with detention and the cane, protest about their school day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frustrated' rearranges DETENTION CANE DUO into T NEED NO EDUCATION. 16 is SOLECISTIC: Pink Floyd's lyric is a double negative.
explanation.definitionFit: The line from Another Brick in the Wall is a famously ungrammatical assertion with its double negative.

clue.text: They're old stories — slippery surface mentioned previously

indicators.note: previously means the sounded piece comes before the stories
mentioned means spoken, so the word for the ice is taken by its sound

parts.note: a rink is a sheet of ice for skating
lies are untrue stories

explanation.surface: Tall tales about a skating rink told earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mentioned' signals a sound-alike: the ice word is spelt with a silent W, and 'previously' puts it ahead of the stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrinklies is British slang for elderly people, from their lined skin.

clue.text: Breaking the rules, one army leader's first to go in

parts.note: sole means one and only

indicators.note: to go in means to be placed inside, so the ordinal sits within the commander's letters

parts.note: CIC is commander-in-chief
1st is first, written with I for the 1

explanation.surface: A commander pushes ahead of his troops, defying regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: IST stands for 1ST with the digit read as I; it goes inside CIC to give CISTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a breach of grammar or etiquette, so solecistic means rule-breaking.

clue.text: Child succeeds before becoming recluse

indicators.note: to succeed is to follow, so the child comes after the other piece

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A child inherits a position before turning into a hermit.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a hermit, especially a Christian one living alone.

clue.text: Prepared to be drawn? Not initially

indicators.note: not initially means without its first letter

parts.note: drawn as in tense and taut means strained

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are ready to be sketched, but not right away.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained person has been prepared or taught for a task.

clue.text: Touch one's bottom when talking

indicators.note: when talking means the words are heard rather than written

parts.note: one is a, and a bottom is a butt

explanation.surface: Mentioning one's backside in conversation, a cheeky remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that abut meet or adjoin along an edge.

clue.text: Say, Peter's head's dropping — he's little time for 16 song

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: the apostle Peter is an example of a saint, giving saint's
the letters used as written
wee is Scots for little
T is time in physics

explanation.surface: An apostle bows his head as a tiny man sings a short song.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is SOLECISTIC: 'ain't' is a nonstandard contraction. The 1927 song is a jazz standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Ain't She Sweet is a popular 1920s song whose title uses the ungrammatical ain't.

clue.text: Say John Lennon's old name out loud

indicators.note: out loud means the name is spoken, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: Liverpool John Lennon Airport was formerly Speke Airport, named after the district

explanation.surface: Asks for the Beatle's former name to be said aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Lennon himself, but it is the airport bearing his name, once called Speke.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak is to say or utter words.

clue.text: Are after man from capital

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated a
then means afterwards
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: Something about being after a man who came from the city.
explanation.definitionFit: An Athenian comes from Athens, the Greek capital.

clue.text: Country militia had to show up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom upwards
to show means to reveal, so the answer is among the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Armed irregulars had to appear in force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to show' finds ITIAH inside MILITIA HAD, and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is a Caribbean nation on Hispaniola.

clue.text: Control party underling

parts.note: a do is a party
a minion is a servile underling

explanation.surface: A party run by a junior functionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominion means sovereignty or authority over something.

clue.text: See 8
Not yet out, largely impress

indicators.note: largely means for the most part, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: a batsman not yet out is in still, that is still batting

explanation.surface: A batsman, still at the crease, mostly makes an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: a batsman who is not out is 'in'; still in, reworded as IN STILL, loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil an idea is to impress it gradually on someone's mind.

clue.text: See 10
4 diners turned into others perhaps

indicators.note: into means the numeral is set inside the other letters
turned means overturned and rearranged, so these letters change order

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four restaurants converted into something different.
explanation.walkthrough: The 4 looks like a reference to 4-down; it is the numeral IV. 'turned' makes DREINS, and 'into' places IV inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive-ins are another kind of eatery besides diners, so they exemplify others.
